entities.name: PMID:25443472
observations: Comparative household study sampled 11,674 environmental sites across 7 CF homes and 8 non-CF homes over 3–8 visits.
Pseudomonas aeruginosa was recovered from 28% of sampled drains at least once; modeled recovery was 6.3% of drain samples, more than eightfold higher than any other household-environment category.
The abstract reports aggregate drains and does not provide separate CF-versus-non-CF or sink-versus-shower-versus-toilet frequencies.

entities.name: PMID:22329595
observations: Environmental study included 47 Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from homes of families with or without children with CF, but did not report recovery frequencies by household location.
Among 23 characterized environmental strains, 14 were exoS-positive and 9 were exoU-positive.

entities.name: PMID:32684992
observations: CF-focused review summarizes household Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolation primarily from shower drains, kitchen and bathroom hand-basin drainpipes, and toilet drainpipes.
This is secondary evidence and provides no denominator or direct CF-versus-non-CF comparison.

entities.name: Household drains predominant
observations: In the main comparative study, drains were the predominant household recovery category across the combined CF and non-CF home sample, with modeled recovery over eightfold higher than from other environmental categories.
Evidence does not establish separate drain prevalence for CF versus non-CF homes.
